Analysis-For-Submission (Revision)

Sarah Lotspeich

2026-07-30

Setup

# Load packages
library(missALI) ## for models x missing data corrections 
library(pROC) ## for ROC curves and AUC 
library(ggplot2) ## for plots (in general)
library(patchwork) ## for multi-panel plots 
library(naniar) ## for upset plots of missing data patterns

# Read in data on hospitalizations (suppressed for privacy)
#hosp_dat = read.csv("~/Documents/missALI/data/deidentified_ali_hospitalizations.csv")
hosp_dat = read.csv("~/Documents/Allostatic_load_audits/revision_analysis_dat.csv") |> 
  ## Exclude one person with no vitals/labs before hospitalization day so all components missing
  filter(!is.na(ALI))

# Define vector of binary ALI component column names
ali_comp <- c("A1C", "ALB", "BMI", "CHOL", "CRP",
              "CREAT_C", "HCST", "TRIG", "BP_DIASTOLIC", "BP_SYSTOLIC")

Exclusions

  • Patients whose first primary care encounters were not at least 90 days before the end of the study period.
  • For patients who were hospitalized, only visits and labs before their hospitalization (at least 1 day but no more than 3 years) were included in the averages used for ALI components.
  • One patient (who was hospitalized) only had vitals and labs on their day of hospitalization, so they were missing all 10 components and had to be excluded.
  • Altogether, these exclusions left us with \(n=\) 707 patients’ data.

Exploratory Data Analysis

Figure 2

Patterns of missingness in the \(10\) allostatic load index (ALI) for the \(n = 1000\) patients in the sample from the electronic health records (EHR) at Atrium Health Wake Forest Baptist Hospital. Each row represents one of the \(18\) distinct missing data patterns, and within that row the ALI component(s) with an ``X’’ were missing.

Figure 3

Distributions of the allostatic load index (ALI) for the \(n = 1000\) patients in the sample from the electronic health records (EHR) at Atrium Health Wake Forest Baptist Hospital after using the complete-case proportion and best/worst case imputation missing data methods.
## # A tibble: 1 × 3
##   CC_PROP_ALI BEST_CASE_ALI WORST_CASE_ALI
##         <dbl>         <dbl>          <dbl>
## 1       0.333           0.2            0.7

Figure 4

Proportion of \(n = 1000\) patients in the sample from the electronic health records (EHR) at Atrium Health Wake Forest Baptist Hospital with healthy, unhealthy, and missing values across the \(10\) allostatic load index (ALI) components, after discretizing the original numeric biomarkers at their clinically meaningful thresholds from Table 1.

Figure 5

Missingness upset plot displaying combinations of allostatic load index (ALI) components that were missing together for patients.

Results

# Create empty dataframe to save AUC for all methods/models
save_auc = data.frame()

Model 1: Logistic Regression

Summary Measure Models

Approach 1: Proportion of Non-Missing Components That Are Unhealthy

Fit to Full Sample
# Logistic regression + complete-case proportion
mod_log_prop = cc_prop_approach(outcome = "ANY_ADMIT", 
                                covar = c("SEX", "AGE_AT_ENCOUNTER"), 
                                ali = ali_comp,
                                data = hosp_dat, 
                                family = "binomial") 

# View the fitted model summary
mod_log_prop$fit |> 
  summary()
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = as.formula(paste(outcome, "~ ", paste(c("PROP_UNHEALTHY", 
##     covar), collapse = "+"))), family = family, data = data)
## 
## Coefficients:
##                  Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)      -3.05458    0.41208  -7.413 1.24e-13 ***
## PROP_UNHEALTHY    1.40547    0.50767   2.769  0.00563 ** 
## SEXMale           0.04813    0.20808   0.231  0.81709    
## AGE_AT_ENCOUNTER  0.01924    0.00804   2.393  0.01669 *  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1)
## 
##     Null deviance: 634.40  on 706  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 615.28  on 703  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 623.28
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 4
# Calculate predicted probabilities
pred_prob_log_prop = mod_log_prop$fit |> 
  predict(type = "response")

# Make the ROC curve 
## Include AUC (95% Confidence Interval)
roc_curve = roc(hosp_dat$ANY_ADMIT, pred_prob_log_prop)
## Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
## Setting direction: controls < cases
roc_log_prop = full_sample_roc(roc_obj = roc_curve, 
                               line_col = miss_meth_cols[1], 
                               method_title = "Complete-Case\nProportion")
roc_log_prop

# Save AUC to dataframe 
save_auc = save_auc |> 
  rbind(
    data.frame(
      Model = "Logistic", 
      Missing = "Complete-Case Proportion",
      Separate_Components = "Summary Measure",
      Fit = "Full-Sample", 
      AUC = auc(roc_curve)
    ))
5-Fold Cross-Validated
# Make fold assignment reproducible (same for all models + approaches)
set.seed(918)

# 5-fold cross validation of the logistic regression model with complete-case proportion ALI
kfold_log_cc_prop = kfold_validate(outcome = "ANY_ADMIT", 
                                   covar = c("SEX", "AGE_AT_ENCOUNTER"), 
                                   ali = ali_comp,
                                   data = hosp_dat, 
                                   family = "binomial", 
                                   miss_method = "cc_prop", 
                                   folds = 5)
## Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
## Setting direction: controls < cases
## Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
## Setting direction: controls < cases
## Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
## Setting direction: controls < cases
## Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
## Setting direction: controls < cases
## Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
## Setting direction: controls < cases
## View AUC from 5 folds 
kfold_log_cc_prop$all_fold_auc
## [1] 0.6816288 0.5549242 0.5647157 0.6568966 0.6080978
median(kfold_log_cc_prop$all_fold_auc) ### summarized by median
## [1] 0.6080978
## Plot individual ROC curves from 5 folds with median over top 
roc_log_prop_k = kfold_log_cc_prop |> 
  kfold_roc(plot_folds = 1:5, 
            overlay_average = TRUE,
            line_col = miss_meth_cols[1]) 
roc_log_prop_k
## `geom_smooth()` using method = 'loess' and formula = 'y ~ x'

# Save AUC to dataframe 
save_auc = save_auc |> 
  rbind(
    data.frame(
      Model = "Logistic", 
      Missing = "Complete-Case Proportion", 
      Separate_Components = "Summary Measure",
      Fit = "K-Fold", 
      AUC = median(kfold_log_cc_prop$all_fold_auc)
    ))

# Random forest + pattern submodels (separate components)
mod_rf_patsub = pattern_submod_approach(outcome = "ANY_ADMIT",
                                        covar = c("SEX", "AGE_AT_ENCOUNTER"),
                                        ali = ali_comp,
                                        data = hosp_dat,
                                        family = "binomial", 
                                        use_glm = FALSE)
## Missing pattern MP-9 (only A1C,ALB,BMI,CHOL,CRP,TRIG,BP_DIASTOLIC,BP_SYSTOLIC observed) was too small and nested within
##    -> Missing pattern MP-1 (only A1C,ALB,BMI,CHOL,TRIG,BP_DIASTOLIC,BP_SYSTOLIC observed).
## Missing pattern MP-10 (only A1C,ALB,BMI,CHOL,HCST,TRIG,BP_DIASTOLIC,BP_SYSTOLIC observed) was too small and nested within
##    -> Missing pattern MP-1 (only A1C,ALB,BMI,CHOL,TRIG,BP_DIASTOLIC,BP_SYSTOLIC observed).
## Missing pattern MP-11 (only ALB,BMI,CHOL,HCST,TRIG,BP_DIASTOLIC,BP_SYSTOLIC observed) was too small and nested within
##    -> Missing pattern MP-2 (only ALB,BMI,CHOL,TRIG,BP_DIASTOLIC,BP_SYSTOLIC observed).
## Missing pattern MP-13 (only ALB,BMI,CHOL,CRP,TRIG,BP_DIASTOLIC,BP_SYSTOLIC observed) was too small and nested within
##    -> Missing pattern MP-2 (only ALB,BMI,CHOL,TRIG,BP_DIASTOLIC,BP_SYSTOLIC observed).
## Missing pattern MP-14 (only ALB,BMI,CREAT_C,BP_DIASTOLIC,BP_SYSTOLIC observed) was too small and nested within
##    -> Missing pattern MP-4 (only ALB,BMI,BP_DIASTOLIC,BP_SYSTOLIC observed).
## Missing pattern MP-15 (only BMI,CHOL,HCST,TRIG,BP_DIASTOLIC,BP_SYSTOLIC observed) was too small and nested within
##    -> Missing pattern MP-3 (only BMI,BP_DIASTOLIC,BP_SYSTOLIC observed).
## Missing pattern MP-16 (only BMI,HCST,BP_DIASTOLIC,BP_SYSTOLIC observed) was too small and nested within
##    -> Missing pattern MP-3 (only BMI,BP_DIASTOLIC,BP_SYSTOLIC observed).
# Calculate predicted probabilities
pred_prob_rf_patsub = mod_rf_patsub |> 
  predict_pattern_submod()

# Make the ROC curve 
## Include AUC (95% Confidence Interval)
roc_curve = roc(hosp_dat$ANY_ADMIT, pred_prob_rf_patsub)
## Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
## Setting direction: controls < cases
roc_rf_submod = full_sample_roc(roc_obj = roc_curve, 
                                 line_col = miss_meth_cols[8], 
                                 method_title = "Pattern\nSubmodels")
roc_rf_submod

# Save AUC to dataframe 
save_auc = save_auc |> 
  rbind(
    data.frame(
      Model = "Random Forest", 
      Missing = "Pattern Submodels", 
      Separate_Components = "Separate Components",
      Fit = "Full-Sample", 
      AUC = auc(roc_curve)
    ))
